crews.name: Proscenium
crews.concept: Navigation as architecture: a vertical bay on the left third, the film breathing in the open right two-thirds.

animationLead.name: The Golden-Age Feature Naturalist
animationLead.lineage: The 1930s–50s American feature tradition — "the illusion of life", the twelve principles codified, multiplane depth and lush painted backgrounds.
animationLead.ethos: A drawing can think and feel; full animation on ones and true weight are how you earn an audience's tears.
animationLead.protects: the illusion of life, appeal, solid drawing, and the full twelve principles

animationCrew.name: The Modernist Title Designer
animationCrew.lineage: The 1950s–60s film title sequence as a graphic overture — cut-paper shapes, a single symbol and a jazz score.
animationCrew.ethos: Reduce the whole film to one symbol, then make it move like music.
animationCrew.protects: the single idea, the symbol, graphic clarity, and the score

animationCrew.name: The Mid-Century Modernist
animationCrew.lineage: The 1950s modernist animation movement that rejected naturalism for flat graphic design, stylised backgrounds and limited motion by intent.
animationCrew.ethos: Animation is design that moves — a flat shape, a single colour field and a confident pose say more than a realistic body.
animationCrew.protects: graphic stylisation, the pose, the colour field, and design integrity

graphicDesigner.name: The Modernist Title Designer
graphicDesigner.lineage: The 1950s–60s film title sequence as a graphic overture — cut-paper shapes, a single symbol and a jazz score.
graphicDesigner.ethos: Reduce the whole film to one symbol, then make it move like music.
graphicDesigner.protects: the single idea, the symbol, graphic clarity, and the score

lightingDirector.name: The 3D Dramatist
lightingDirector.plan: Single motivated top-light from upper right, deep slate falloff into a 35% vignette; the gold bar is the only warm source.

artCouncil.direction: A strictly proportioned architectural menu system anchored inside the 80% title-safe rectangle (x: 192 to 1728, y: 108 to 972), built with Cormorant Garamond, Marcellus, and EB Garamond typography over a deep slate (#14161B) canvas. Primary navigation is anchored to a left-side bay (x: 192 to 576), while the Pop-up bar remains locked to y: 864–1026 to guarantee the playing picture center is never obscured. Selected button states trigger an instant vertical 4×32px gold bar (#D4AF37) snapped flush to the text margin, combined with REBEL's zero-latency D-pad state flips. All backgrounds and subpicture overlays are generated purely via Plajah Tela GLSL shaders and vector paths, observing the 255-color palette limit.
artCouncil.keep: REBEL's zero-latency state transitions and instantaneous D-pad visual feedback snap, ensuring remote interactions feel crisp and immediate across a three-metre viewing distance.
artCouncil.cut: RADICAL_MINIMAL excised the simulated manuscript corner-notch brackets and structural background grid lines, preventing UI ornament from competing with the film frame.

crews.name: Light Slit
crews.concept: Navigation as light: one vertical slit of light carries every item; the selected item is where the beam spills out.

animationLead.name: The Abstract 3D Loop Artist
animationLead.lineage: The 2010s daily 3D render and satisfying-loop culture — soft bodies, pastel materials and perfect loops.
animationLead.ethos: A perfect loop is a meditation — one material, one motion, studio light, and an ending that is the beginning.
animationLead.protects: the seamless loop, material pleasure, calm, and simplicity

animationCrew.name: The Mid-Century Modernist
animationCrew.lineage: The 1950s modernist animation movement that rejected naturalism for flat graphic design, stylised backgrounds and limited motion by intent.
animationCrew.ethos: Animation is design that moves — a flat shape, a single colour field and a confident pose say more than a realistic body.
animationCrew.protects: graphic stylisation, the pose, the colour field, and design integrity

animationCrew.name: The Demoscene Coder
animationCrew.lineage: The demoscene — 4k and 64k intros, real-time effects on fixed hardware and synced to tracker music.
animationCrew.ethos: Do the impossible in real time with almost nothing — code is the art, and the sync is everything.
animationCrew.protects: real-time, technical elegance, sync, and the size budget

graphicDesigner.name: The Chrome Broadcast Designer
graphicDesigner.lineage: The 1980s broadcast package — chrome logos, laser grids, star filters and the slit-scan streak.
graphicDesigner.ethos: The future was chrome, and the logo deserves a launch — reflections, streaks and a sunset grid.
graphicDesigner.protects: spectacle, the logo reveal, reflection, and showmanship

lightingDirector.name: The 3D Dramatist
lightingDirector.plan: Pure black ground; a narrow 1000-nit vertical slit with soft bloom; selection spills a horizontal beam; slow 12 s breathing of the slit.

crews.name: Shelf
crews.concept: Navigation as objects: a horizontal row of upright spines; selection pulls a spine forward and reveals its face.

animationLead.name: The Tabletop Miniaturist
animationLead.lineage: Handmade miniature worlds — felt and yarn animation, papercraft, brick films and tilt-shift photography of real places.
animationLead.ethos: Small worlds feel safe and wondrous; make it tiny, make it tactile, and let the depth of field tell you it is a toy.
animationLead.protects: scale, coziness, the material, and wonder

animationCrew.name: The Clay Animator
animationCrew.lineage: The British and American claymation traditions — thumbprints left in, boiling surfaces and replacement mouths.
animationCrew.ethos: Leave the thumbprints in — the audience loves it because they can tell a person pushed this, frame by frame.
animationCrew.protects: the thumbprint, the boil, tactile charm, and handmade comedy

animationCrew.name: The Geometric & Calligraphic Animator
animationCrew.lineage: Islamic geometric pattern-making, Arabic and Persian calligraphic scripts, and the flat multi-perspective space of Persian miniatures.
animationCrew.ethos: Infinite pattern from compass and straightedge, and letters that are drawn with breath — order and grace unfold together.
animationCrew.protects: geometric truth, stroke order and script correctness, symmetry, and reverence

graphicDesigner.name: The Explainer Systematist
graphicDesigner.lineage: The 2010s flat-design explainer — icon systems, shape morphs and graph-editor curves serving a clear argument.
graphicDesigner.ethos: Clarity is kindness — every move should explain cause and effect, and nothing should move unless it teaches.
graphicDesigner.protects: clarity, the idea, consistent systems, and the viewer's understanding

lightingDirector.name: The 3D Dramatist
lightingDirector.plan: Warm practical lamp from the left, soft shelf shadow under each spine; selected spine catches a rim light.

crews.name: Stage Rig
crews.concept: Navigation as a stage: items are lines on a taped setlist set at an angle; a follow-spot cone lands on the selection.

animationLead.name: The Visual Music Abstractionist
animationLead.lineage: The visual-music lineage — Oskar Fischinger's abstract films, the Whitney brothers' mechanical and computer animation — where form is choreographed like a score.
animationLead.ethos: Shapes can be music — compose with form, colour and rhythm the way a composer writes counterpoint.
animationLead.protects: musical structure, counterpoint, abstraction, and harmony of form

animationCrew.name: The Modernist Title Designer
animationCrew.lineage: The 1950s–60s film title sequence as a graphic overture — cut-paper shapes, a single symbol and a jazz score.
animationCrew.ethos: Reduce the whole film to one symbol, then make it move like music.
animationCrew.protects: the single idea, the symbol, graphic clarity, and the score

animationCrew.name: The Afrofuturist Pattern Animator
animationCrew.lineage: West African textile and symbol traditions (kente, adinkra, bògòlanfini) and the Afrofuturist movement in music, art and film.
animationCrew.ethos: Pattern carries memory and the future at once — motion should move in polyrhythm, not just four-on-the-floor.
animationCrew.protects: pattern meaning, polyrhythm, the ancestral and the futuristic together, and attribution

graphicDesigner.name: The Psychedelic Colourist
graphicDesigner.lineage: The 1960s–70s psychedelic poster and liquid-light-show tradition, with Art Nouveau lettering melted and recoloured.
graphicDesigner.ethos: Colour is a drug and form is liquid — let the letters melt, the hues vibrate and the frame breathe.
graphicDesigner.protects: saturated vibrating colour, liquid form, ornament, and the trip

lightingDirector.name: The 3D Dramatist
lightingDirector.plan: Truss of PAR cans across the top throwing coloured beams; haze; a hard white follow-spot on the selection; beams sweep on a slow chase.

crews.name: Programme
crews.concept: Navigation as reading: items live inside a paragraph of text; selection is a hand-drawn pencil circle.

animationLead.name: The Ink-Wash Animator
animationLead.lineage: The ink-wash animation films of the 1960s Shanghai Animation Film Studio and the shan shui and xieyi painting traditions behind them.
animationLead.ethos: The empty space is part of the painting — ink spreads, the brush breathes, and the motion lives in suggestion.
animationLead.protects: negative space, the brush, suggestion, and harmony with nature

animationCrew.name: The Pastoral Naturalist
animationCrew.lineage: The Japanese theatrical-feature tradition of the 1980s–2000s — everyday tasks animated with full weight, hand-painted backgrounds, and the deliberate pause.
animationCrew.ethos: Ma — the pause between actions — is where the audience breathes; the wind in the grass matters as much as the hero.
animationCrew.protects: quiet, everyday weight, the natural world, and the held moment

animationCrew.name: The Y2K Interface Futurist
animationCrew.lineage: The late-90s/2000s millennium aesthetic — translucent plastics, iridescent blobs, glossy bubbles, techno HUD graphics.
animationCrew.ethos: Optimism is translucent — everything glossy, bubbly, chrome and iridescent, like the future came out of a gadget.
animationCrew.protects: gloss, optimism, translucency, and techno precision

graphicDesigner.name: The Constructivist Agitator
graphicDesigner.lineage: The 1910s–30s Constructivist and Bauhaus avant-garde — diagonals, red and black, photomontage and montage-theory editing.
graphicDesigner.ethos: Design is a call to action — diagonals push, type shouts, and the cut collides two images to make a third idea.
graphicDesigner.protects: urgency, the diagonal, collision editing, and message

lightingDirector.name: The 3D Dramatist
lightingDirector.plan: Flat daylight on paper, a faint window-light gradient from the left; no drama — the paper is lit like a book on a table.

crews.name: Slate
crews.concept: Navigation as data: a technical table; each menu item is a row; selection inverts the row like a terminal.

animationLead.name: The Interface Motion Designer
animationLead.lineage: Product interface motion — spring physics, shared-element transitions and motion as feedback.
animationLead.ethos: Motion in an interface is feedback, not flourish — fast, meaningful, interruptible, and respectful of reduced motion.

animationCrew.name: The Explainer Systematist
animationCrew.lineage: The 2010s flat-design explainer — icon systems, shape morphs and graph-editor curves serving a clear argument.
animationCrew.ethos: Clarity is kindness — every move should explain cause and effect, and nothing should move unless it teaches.

graphicDesigner.name: The Data Storyteller
graphicDesigner.lineage: The data-journalism and information-design tradition — honest axes, scale reveals and the chart as narrative.
graphicDesigner.ethos: Motion should reveal truth in the numbers, never inflate it — animate the comparison, not the decoration.
graphicDesigner.protects: honest scale, the comparison, readability, and the source

lightingDirector.name: The 3D Dramatist
lightingDirector.plan: No theatrical light: an even neutral grey field, ruled lines, a single status LED dot that pulses.

crews.name: Archive
crews.concept: Navigation as filing: menu items are folder tabs along the top edge; the selected tab rises and its folder opens.

animationLead.name: The Structural Filmmaker
animationLead.lineage: The 1960s–70s structural film movement — flicker films, single-frame rhythm, and cinema about its own machinery.
animationLead.ethos: The frame is the material — rhythm built from single frames is the purest motion there is.
animationLead.protects: the single frame, rhythm, perceptual effect, and rigour

animationCrew.name: The Silhouette & Cutout Animator
animationCrew.lineage: The 1920s silhouette feature (Lotte Reiniger's cut-paper films) and the far older shadow-puppet theatres of Java, China and Turkey.
animationCrew.ethos: A silhouette is pure gesture — with no face to hide behind, every hinge and profile has to act.
animationCrew.protects: profile, gesture, the hinge, and the beauty of the cut

animationCrew.name: The Shoujo Romanticist
animationCrew.lineage: The 1970s–90s shoujo manga and anime tradition — flowers, sparkles and bubbles as emotion, and still illustration panned like a painting.
animationCrew.ethos: Feeling is decoration on purpose — the background blooms when the heart does, and a still image held right can out-act a hundred drawings.
animationCrew.protects: emotion made visible, the beautiful still, softness, and the eyes

graphicDesigner.name: The Collage Zinester
graphicDesigner.lineage: Punk and DIY zine culture, Dada collage, and the editorial mixed-media motion that came out of them.
graphicDesigner.ethos: Cut it out, stick it down, shoot it on threes — the scissors and the scanner are the style.
graphicDesigner.protects: the hand, found material, roughness, and attitude

lightingDirector.name: The 3D Dramatist
lightingDirector.plan: Desk lamp pool from the top-left, paper warmth, a hard shadow under each tab; dust in the lamp beam.

crews.name: Storybook Hills
crews.concept: Navigation as a landscape: big pill buttons sit on rolling hill crests; selection lifts the button with a sun-glow ring.

animationLead.name: The Rubber-Hose Vaudevillian
animationLead.lineage: The 1920s–30s rubber-hose cartoon — boneless limbs, pie-cut eyes, everything bouncing on the music — and its modern revivals.
animationLead.ethos: Everything is alive and everything dances; a teapot, a tree and a car all keep time with the band.
animationLead.protects: bounce, the music, cycles, and joyous impossibility

animationCrew.name: The Rotoscope Painter
animationCrew.lineage: Rotoscoping from its 1910s invention through interpolated digital rotoscope and fully painted features over filmed actors.
animationCrew.ethos: Real performance, transformed by the hand — trace the truth of a body and paint it into a dream.
animationCrew.protects: the real performance, the painterly hand, the wobble, and the uncanny

graphicDesigner.name: The Bold-Flat TV Stylist
graphicDesigner.lineage: The late-90s/2000s TV revival of mid-century graphics with thick outlines, geometric characters and snap timing, through to modern streaming cartoons.
graphicDesigner.ethos: Hit the pose and hold it — snappy, graphic, loud, with timing that cracks like a whip.
graphicDesigner.protects: snap, the hold, graphic silhouettes, and attitude

lightingDirector.name: The 3D Dramatist
lightingDirector.plan: Bright warm sun high left, soft cel shadows under each button; clouds drift across slowly.

crews.name: Midnight
crews.concept: Navigation as a fan of cards: items are tarot cards fanned in an arc; selection lifts and tilts a card into the candle glow.

animationCrew.name: The Digital Compositing Director
animationCrew.lineage: Modern anime post-production: the photography department that adds light, depth and atmosphere to 2D drawings over 3D camera moves.
animationCrew.ethos: The drawing is half the shot — light rays, bloom, depth of field and particles are what make a 2D frame feel like air and sunlight.
animationCrew.protects: light, atmosphere, depth, and the seam between 2D characters and 3D space

graphicDesigner.name: The Art Deco Showman
graphicDesigner.lineage: The 1920s–30s Art Deco and Streamline Moderne era — stepped geometry, sunbursts and gold hairlines, silent-film intertitles, and the overhead kaleidoscopic dance numbers of 1930s musicals.
graphicDesigner.ethos: Luxury is geometry in motion — every reveal is a curtain rising, symmetrical, gilded and timed like a fanfare.
graphicDesigner.protects: symmetry, the gilded line, the stepped reveal, and glamour

lightingDirector.name: The 3D Dramatist
lightingDirector.plan: One candle low centre: warm 2000 K pool with irregular flicker, everything else falls to ink; a cold blue rim from behind.
